statement: If a path law satisfies X_n dot l -> +infinity almost surely, then q_L=P(T^-_L<T^+_L) tends to zero as L->infinity, where T^-_L is first hit of {x:x dot l<=-L} and T^+_L first hit of {x:x dot l>=L}.
assumptions: Any probability law on real-valued path projections; no iid, Markov or ellipticity assumption required.
proof_or_counterexample: For each transient path inf_n X_n dot l is finite; hence indicators of T^-_L<infinity decrease to zero. The slab-back-exit indicator is bounded above by them. Apply bounded convergence.
remaining_gap: No quantitative decay of q_L; the proposed scale-doubling recursion is unproved and depends on unavailable decoupling.
status: proved special case; independent check pending

statement: For any quenched nearest-neighbor kernel on Z^d with each transition >=kappa and escape radius of S <= integer r, P_x(T_S>mr)<=(1-kappa^r)^m and E_x T_S<=r/kappa^r; same conditional tail from a finite stopping time for a set chosen then and held fixed.
assumptions: d>=1; 0<kappa<=1/(2d); proper S; no iid or transience needed.
source_quote: At any block time mr on {T_S>mr}, choose a shortest lattice path ... its length s is at most r.
proof_or_counterexample: At each actual block boundary conditional success probability is >=kappa^r. Iterate conditional expectations, then sum in r-blocks. No independence or future-event conditioning used.
remaining_gap: Single residence does not control returns or directional regeneration time.

statement: For finite nonempty S in Z^d with N sites, its escape radius r(S) obeys r(S)^d<=d!N; ER then bounds its first exit time by R kappa^-R with R=floor((d!N)^(1/d)).
assumptions: d>=1; finite S; kappa-uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor kernel for exit-time consequence.
source_quote: Stars and bars counts binom(r(S)-1+d,d) such points.
proof_or_counterexample: At a depth-r site the nonnegative orthant simplex of radius r-1 lies in S and has binomial count >=r^d/d!; apply ER at integer R.
remaining_gap: No iid probability estimate for a selected large trap; no parent implication.

statement: For adaptive fixed-during-residence sets of escape radius <=r and any positive integer random horizon tau finite on B with P(B)=p>0, K_tau=min{m>=1:sigma_m>=tau} satisfies E[K_tau|B]<=E[tau|B]<=ceil(8r log(4/3)/kappa^r)(E[K_tau|B]+3/p).
assumptions: Quenched nearest-neighbor transitions >=kappa; episode sets chosen at stopping times and held fixed; tau and B may be future-dependent; r>=1 integer.
source_quote: K_tau<=m then tau<=sigma_m, regardless of whether tau is a stopping time.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently reproduced conditional geometric mgf <=4/3, tower bound for sigma_m, Chernoff with one division by p, and L-block tail sum; details in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: Need E[K_tau|B]<infinity for actual RWRE regeneration horizon; CC alone does not give it.

statement: For each fixed kappa<1/4, homogeneous planar iid kappa-elliptic walks with drift 2delta e1 are ballistic, yet their Green expectation at zero is unbounded as delta decreases to zero; each fixed delta>0 has finite Green expectation.
source_quote: The obstruction is to a uniform or purely local inference, not to each law separately.
proof_or_counterexample: Independent fair-sign transform at delta=0 gives central-binomial squared return bound; likelihood ratio preserves half of first N returns for delta<=1/(16N); exponential tilt proves fixed-delta finiteness.
remaining_gap: Does not rule out fixed-law integrability or C0041.

statement: If all finite connected killed-Green auxiliary kernels of an iid UE nearest-neighbor RWRE have drift >=delta>0 in unit direction l, then condition (T) holds near l; hence the known (T) implication gives deterministic ballistic velocity v with v dot l>=delta and E H_L<=(L+1)/delta.
assumptions: d>=2; site-iid UE; finite-domain auxiliary rows defined from occupation-weighted Green functions; uniform extra drift premise over all finite connected domains and sites.
source: ~/brain_workers/w448/SPECIAL_CASE.md; Drewitz-Ramirez arXiv:1309.2589 Definition 3.13 and (T') ballisticity discussion
source_quote: The auxiliary killed chain has a finite Green matrix. Its occupation vector is the unique solution of these equations
proof_or_counterexample: Verified occupation flow uniqueness and boundary flux equality, exponential supermartingale, finite slab exhaustion, and half-space first-passage moment. Standard (T) implication imported at stated IID+UE+d>=2 scope.
remaining_gap: No derivation of the extra uniform auxiliary drift from bare transience; parent C0041 not solved by this criterion.
status: proved special case; independently checked conditional proof

statement: For the two-row iid law A=(7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10), B=(1/10,7/10,1/10,1/10), A-mass a>7/8 implies auxiliary e1 drift at least (3/5)(a-7(1-a))/(a+7(1-a)); at a=9/10 the lower bound is 3/40. At a=11/20 and U={0,-e1}, raw drift is 3/50 but auxiliary origin drift is -606/10105.
assumptions: Z^2 nearest-neighbor site-iid; kappa=1/10; finite connected domains for bound; two-site U for negative-tilt calculation; no transience claim for a=11/20.
proof_or_counterexample: Independently derived G_U(0,x)=h/w_type by first-arrival and return decomposition; ratio bound yields delta. Exact four-type-pair enumeration via python -X utf8 verify_peer_arithmetic.py produced 3/50, 2021/1581, -202/2635, -606/10105 and 3/40.
remaining_gap: Positive example has an extra one-site-law assumption; negative example says nothing about directional transience; neither proves parent.
status: proved special cases; independently checked proof

target: w446 finite-region visit and time tails
statement: For D finite inside S={x:0<=x1<=N-1}, m=|D|>=1, tau=tau_D∧tau_S, and a_N(y+e1)>=a>0 for each y in D, a quenched kappa-uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor walk satisfies P(V_y>=k)<=(1-kappa*a)^(k-1) for k>=1 and P(tau>t)<=m(1-kappa*a)^(ceil((t+1)/m)-1) for integer t>=0.
assumptions: Fixed quenched environment; every nearest-neighbor step probability >=kappa>0; relative-height crossing a_N from y+e1; D finite and nonempty inside S; V_y=sum_{n<tau}1{X_n=y}.
source_quote: At any visit to y before tau, the chance of the prescribed first step y to y+e1 is at least kappa.
proof_or_counterexample: At each visit conditional success probability to leave S before returning to y is >=kappa*a; strong Markov at successive visit times gives geometric tail. Pigeonhole over t+1 times in D and union bound give time tail. Full derivation in REVIEW_PACKET.md.
remaining_gap: No estimate that the per-site a_N lower bound holds at adaptive sites with high environment probability; no parent proof.
